title: Representative Training Notes: Credit for an Earlier Advance Beneficiary Notice, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
## Representative training notes — earlier advance notices on the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program

On the CGM Original Medicare Program, a Medicare advance beneficiary notice (form CMS-R-131) the customer signed earlier for the CGM supply allowance (item A4239) can be credited, as a number of units taken off what a new notice for that item covers. The credit turns on the dates of the customer's CGM refills and on the closing of the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program (its status, closure reason and closed date).

**The governing clause.** This credit takes off the notice the units an earlier advance notice (form CMS-R-131) for the item already covers, only when the customer has stopped insulin and the insulin pharmacy program carries a closed date, a liability notice of any other type never being credited: when the latest such notice was signed after the latest refill of the item shipped and on or after that closed date, its units are taken off; when it was signed on or after that closed date but on or before the latest refill shipped, fewer than 12 whole calendar months before today, its units beyond that refill's units are taken off; otherwise, and whenever the customer has not stopped insulin or the closed date is not recorded, nothing is taken off.

Whole calendar months from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day.

**Which notice is "the latest such notice"?**
The signed form CMS-R-131 notice for item A4239 on the program with the latest signing date. Its units are the billing units it covers. A signed liability notice of any other type is never read for the credit.

**When has the customer stopped insulin here, and what is the closed date?**
The customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is closed with closure reason "customer discontinued"; the closed date is the closed date recorded on that program. A program that is active, on hold or not yet active, or closed for any other reason (for example "changed supplier"), means the customer has not stopped insulin, and nothing is taken off. A program closed with closure reason "customer discontinued" whose closed date is not recorded gives no credit either: nothing is taken off.

**How much is taken off under each branch?**
Under the first branch, all of the earlier notice's units. Under the second, its units beyond the latest CGM refill's units: its units less that refill's units, and nothing when that refill's units are as many or more. Under the third, nothing.

**How do the branches sit side by side?**

| Customer has stopped insulin, closed date recorded | Earlier CMS-R-131 notice signed | Also required | Units taken off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | After the latest refill's ship date, and on or after the insulin pharmacy closed date | — | All of its units |
| Yes | On or after the insulin pharmacy closed date, and on or before the latest refill's ship date | Fewer than 12 whole calendar months before today | Its units beyond the latest refill's units |
| Yes | On or after the closed date, on or before the latest refill, 12 or more whole calendar months before today | — | 0 |
| Yes | Before the insulin pharmacy closed date, or no CMS-R-131 notice signed | — | 0 |
| Stopped insulin, but no closed date recorded | Any date, or none | — | 0 |
| Not stopped insulin | Any date, or none | — | 0 |

**Worked questions (hypothetical figures).** Suppose the customer's insulin pharmacy program closed, closure reason "customer discontinued", on a hypothetical 10 January, that date being recorded as the program's closed date.

- An earlier notice for 9 units was signed on 20 February, after the latest refill shipped on 5 February: all 9 units are taken off.
- An earlier notice for 9 units was signed on 5 February, the same day the latest refill of 7 units shipped: it was not signed after that refill, so the second branch applies; if the signing is fewer than 12 whole calendar months before today, 9 less 7, that is 2 units, are taken off.
- The same notice was for 5 units against that 7-unit refill: it has no units beyond the refill's, so nothing is taken off.
- Whole months: from a hypothetical 5 February to 4 February of the following year is 12 less 1, that is 11 whole calendar months, fewer than 12; to 5 February of the following year is 12, not fewer than 12.
- An earlier notice signed on 8 January, before the 10 January closed date: nothing is taken off.
- The insulin pharmacy program is still active, and a CMS-R-131 notice for 9 units was signed after the latest refill: the customer has not stopped insulin, so nothing is taken off.
